headline: CRUDE RUNS TO $96 AS BEANS SLIP AGAIN
lead: Crude added 2.3% to $96.13 on Iran war-fear headlines out of the UN General Assembly, the same Hormuz cycle that's flared and cooled twice since April, and diesel-hungry harvest crews are the ones who pay for it.
teaser: Crude runs to $96.13 on Iran headlines while beans slip to $12.98 on empty China news.

one_number.unit: barrels per day, Middle East crude exports
one_number.context: Kpler data show Mideast exports rebounded to a fresh high this month, Saudi flows redirected east, undercutting the case that Hormuz risk is actually choking supply.

action: Diesel-dependent harvest budgets: crude above $96.13 and running, lock fuel needs now rather than wait for a pullback that may not come.

sections.title: Crude Runs On Iran Fear
sections.body:
- WTI added 2.3% to **$96.13** after President Trump rejected Iran's UN peace proposal, reviving the same Hormuz risk that gained and deflated twice since April.
- Kpler's 12.8 million bpd Mideast export number says the oil is still moving, this is a headline trade, not a supply shock yet.
sections.so_what: Fuel bills for corn harvest just got more expensive on a headline, not a barrel.

sections.title: Beans Slip On Empty China News
sections.body:
- Soybeans fell 1% to **$12.98**, meal down 1.1%, on what traders are calling "chipped China": no fresh purchase confirmations to offset the August 12 WASDE's bigger crop.
- The $17 billion China purchase commitment hasn't produced a new headline in days, and the board is pricing that silence.
sections.so_what: No news is bad news right now for beans; the rally needs a fresh China.

outside_the_pit.title: Santa Teresa Livestock Port Reopens To Trade
outside_the_pit.body: Another Mexican port resumes cattle trade ahead of the Aug 24 screwworm-reopening framework's next phase, one more data point on returning feeder supply.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress; corn harvest pace above last year's mark says no yield drag story is building.
Crude above $98.50 on fresh Iran headlines keeps the diesel premium in harvest budgets.
A confirmed China soybean purchase over 300K MT is the catalyst beans need to hold $12.98.
